summary: Discovery focused on hosting options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), key management (BYOK, HSM, AWS KMS integration), audit logging and retention, and compliance evidence (SOC 2 / ISO). Customer is evaluating Redwood for production inference for payment fraud models and needs strong controls for keys, logs, and access. Action items: share certs, architecture diagram, schedule POC benchmarks.
topics: Introductions; current stack and risk profile; SOC 2/ISO posture & necessary artifacts; SSO/SAML and RBAC requirements; KMS/BYOK options and HSM; audit logs and SIEM forwarding; data retention and token logging; Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision tradeoffs; next steps and procurement timeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Samira (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for squeezing us in. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on the account. Diego (SE) is here for technical. Quick intros?
[00:12] Aisha (CISO): Aisha Khan, CISO at CinderPoint. We're leading the security review.
[00:18] Ben (Infra): Ben Carter, infra engineer, owns clusters and network.
[00:22] Priya (Product): Priya Nair, product owner for fraud detection.
[00:27] Diego (SE): Hey all, Diego Ramos, solutions engineering, I focus on hosting and key management.
[00:33] Samira: Great. Our goal: understand your compliance gates and how you'd like keys/logs handled. Aisha, can you give us the top must-haves?
[00:41] Aisha: Sure. SOC 2 Type II is table-stakes. We're also mapping to ISO 27001. We need SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC enforced at token and project level, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk) with at least 1 year retention, and BYOK or HSM for production keys. Also, data residency concerns — production inference has EU and NA datastores.
[01:05] Samira: Perfect, that's very aligned with what we've seen. We can do Hosted for early evals, Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private for full isolation and private control plane. Diego, do you want to sketch KMS options?
[01:18] Diego: Yeah. So options: 1) Hosted + Redwood-managed keys (fastest) 2) BYOK with cloud KMS — e.g., AWS KMS/GCP CMEK integrated — where customer retains key control in their cloud 3) Dedicated with HSM add-on where keys are managed in an HSM and we support HSM-backed signing for secrets. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS via IAM roles and also on-prem HSMs — for air-gapped we can mount a bring-your-own-hsm connector. There are some nuance — e.g., TTLs for model cache shards, we don't persist plaintext tokens, but we do persist minimal metadata.
[01:55] Ben: When you say BYOK integrated with AWS KMS, is Redwood able to do envelope encryption so the root CMK never leaves our account?
[02:04] Diego: Yes. Envelope encryption pattern. The CMK stays in your account; we use a data key that is encrypted with your CMK. We rotate per your policy. For Dedicated we can also offer HSM-backed KMS for FIPS compliance.
[02:18] Aisha: And for keys used during inference — are you ever decrypting model weights or cache with Redwood-managed secrets? This is critical for our compliance review.
[02:29] Diego: We don't hold unencrypted customer secrets for longer than necessary. For Private, you can keep keys in your network and we call them via a secure channel. For Dedicated/Hosted we can offer a BYOK flow where the data key is fetched transiently; decrypted memory is wiped after use. There's also an HSM option so the key operation never exposes raw key material to the host.
[02:50] Priya: On the product side, latency's important — fraud scoring is on the critical path. Does BYOK or HSM add latency?
[02:59] Diego: Minimal. Envelope decryption adds a tiny RTT on first use; we cache decrypted data keys in secure memory (and enforce TTLs). HSM operations can be slightly slower than KMS, but often within a few ms. We can benchmark with your prompt shapes.
[03:17] Samira: Let's capture that — Ben, can you share the p95 latency SLO and throughput you need?
[03:23] Ben: We're aiming for p95 under 150ms for scoring and about 120 qps during peak batch windows.
[03:29] Diego: Good, sounds doable with Dedicated pool. For Hosted we'd want to run a test as performance is more variable.
[03:37] Aisha: On audit logs: we need all API calls, admin actions, key usage, and model version changes captured and shipped to Splunk. Retention 1 year on logs in our environment and 90 days in Redwood. Is forwarding possible?
[03:50] Diego: Yes. We support push to customer SIEM via secure log streaming — syslog over TLS or an S3 bucket you control with lifecycle rules. We can also provide discrete audit trails in the console with export. For Hosted customers we maintain an audit log with configurable retention.
[04:05] Aisha: What about token logging? We cannot have PII in any persisted logs.
[04:12] Diego: Agreed. We have redaction filters and an opt-out for request/response logging. By default we keep only hash pointers and non-PII metadata: request size, model id, latency. You can enable or disable request_body retention per route.
[04:28] Marcus (DevOps): If we go Private, would there be a separate control plane? We need provisioning to happen from our network.
[04:35] Diego: For Private, you get a customer-controlled control plane endpoint. Provisioning and management traffic can be routed over your VPC peering or private link. We can deploy the runtime in your VPC or on-prem.
[04:45] Ben: And for upgrades and rollouts, does Redwood push changes or do we control rollouts?
[04:51] Samira: Rollouts are configurable. For Private, you can choose to accept updates, or opt into managed updates. For Dedicated we manage the runtime but provide canary controls and automatic fallback to a previous model.
[05:02] Priya: For compliance evidence, we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 reports, as well as pen test results and an AUP. Can you provide those?
[05:11] Samira: Yes — we'll share links to SOC 2 Type II, ISO artifacts, and our security whitepaper. I'll put them in the follow-up thread.
[05:18] Aisha: Also need details on encryption at rest: keys, disk, and backups.
[05:24] Diego: At rest we use AES-256. Disk encryption is enabled for storage volumes. Backups are encrypted with your KMS if BYOK; otherwise Redwood-managed keys encrypted with our KMS. For Dedicated we can configure customer keys for backups.
[05:36] Aisha: Data residency — can you confine inference and logs to EU region? We cannot have PII leave EU for some workflows.
[05:45] Diego: Absolutely. We support region pinning per project. We can pin models and inference to eu-west-1 and forward audit logs to your EU SIEM endpoint. For Hosted customers we have region options; Dedicated allows you to reserve capacity in a region; Private allows full control.
[06:00] Ben: How do you handle secrets for service accounts? We need SAML + SCIM and ensure least privilege when issuing tokens to apps.
[06:08] Samira: We support SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC maps to roles and projects; tokens can be short-lived and scoped to routes. Admin actions are gated by RBAC and 2-step approval can be configured.
[06:21] Aisha: Will you provide a list of supported SAML attributes and SCIM mappings?
[06:26] Diego: Yes, we'll include an integration spec. We'll also include an example SAML metadata file.
[06:31] Priya: On retention, we have internal policy: model inputs with possible PII must be retained no longer than 30 days and must be deletable on request. Can Redwood support per-route retention and delete-on-demand?
[06:43] Diego: We support per-route retention settings and a deletion API that supports bulk remove. For Hosted, we keep retention configurable — default 90 days — but we can set down to 0 for request bodies. For Dedicated/Private you get more control and we can set retention to match your policy.
[06:59] Ben: For the POC, we'd like a test harness and a way to run our prompt set against a dedicated small pool with BYOK and audit forwarding enabled. Is that doable?
[07:08] Diego: Totally. We can stand up a small Dedicated pool for POC with BYOK and Splunk forwarding. We'll need your prompts, a sample dataset (sanitized), and definitions of throughput targets. We'll run a two-hour benchmark and share token-level breakdown.
[07:24] Aisha: One more — third-party risk: do you have a subprocessor list and do you sign data processing agreements (DPA)?
[07:32] Samira: Yes — we'll send our subprocessors list and standard DPA; enterprise customers can negotiate terms.
[07:38] Priya: Do you have an SLA for Dedicated? We need 99.9% with latency targets.
[07:43] Samira: Dedicated has SLA tiers — we can share the SLA PDF. For Private on-prem, SLA depends on the support tier.
[07:51] Marcus: Anything else on network? We prefer VPC peering over public endpoints.
[07:56] Diego: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and IP allowlists. For Hosted we do secure ingress and egress with mTLS.
[08:05] Ben: Are logs tamper-evident? We need WORM or append-only for compliance.
[08:11] Diego: We provide immutability options for audit logs in an S3 bucket with Object Lock, or we can stream to your append-only store.
[08:20] Samira: Great. I'll recap next steps. We'll share SOC/ISO artifacts, DPA and subprocessor list, and Diego will draft the private deployment diagram and POC plan. We'll also propose pricing for Dedicated + HSM.
[08:35] Aisha: Timeline-wise, we want a procurement decision by end of Q1 2027. Does that align with Redwood's POC turnaround?
[08:44] Samira: Yes — we can do POC in Jan and have procurement in March.
[08:49] Ben: Ok, we'll send the prompt set and latency targets this week.
[08:54] Priya: And we'll confirm internal stakeholders and timeline.
[08:58] Samira: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and a proposed POC slot.
[09:04] Diego: Thanks, bye.
[09:06] (call ends)
